reviews.text: Prepare to be drawn into the deeply moving drama created by Song’s atmospheric world.
reviews.author: Tanzim Pardiwalla

reviews.text: Celine Song's debut film is a powerful metaphor for the two selves that exist within immigrants.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: Celine Song announces herself as a major voice in cinema with Past Lives, her divine and complex reflection on enduring love.
reviews.author: William Stottor

reviews.text: It is a heartbreaking film that is so masterfully made and profoundly sincere that you want to stay in its world regardless of the emotional cost.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: As the credits roll and we’re given a moment to think about the movie in retrospect, it all just… hits different. And it’s what makes “Past Lives” all the more remarkable as a movie about the bittersweet intensity of love and longing.
reviews.author: Ankit Ojha

reviews.text: Song composes this lyrical, melancholic film with the confidence of a director at the height of their career...[finding] pathos in the potentially mundane creases of a marital bed and a poor internet connection.
reviews.author: Connor Lightbody

reviews.text: Past Lives is a film that leaves you breathless, and your heart aching, but in a good way. There’s something deeply comforting about knowing these feelings are universal.
reviews.author: Joonatan Itkonen

reviews.text: The characters are empty enough for me to imagine my own heartache in its own stead, but hazy characterisations and intriguing concepts aren’t enough to sustain a movie.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: The concept of In-Yun promises that after 8,000 years of connecting, they can marry and be together. Nora and Hae Sun are one life closer.
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: Told with remarkable economy, and perfect performances...
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: Hae Sung in "Past Lives" barely even exists beyond his nostalgic fixation on Nora, and Nora herself is only slightly more well-defined as a character because she has two relationships and the other characters only one.
reviews.author: William Schwartz

reviews.text: The writing was like poetry, I would highly recommend
reviews.author: Andrew Galdi

reviews.text: There’s so much to dig into and relate to, regardless of your background. Past Lives is quietly devastating.
reviews.author: Shadan Larki

reviews.text: Celine Song’s Past Lives calls out to tired souls. It’s a beautifully made anti-fairytale movie, where the prince and the princess meet at the wrong place and time...
reviews.author: Jaylan Salah

reviews.text: To say too much about what happens in each episode would be to spoil the joy of encountering Song’s finely worked screenplay, which lets its characters' emotions glitter in the light.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: In this extraordinary Academy Award-nominated film “Past Lives,” the Korean concept of inyeon is used to lead viewers into believing that Nora and Hae-sung are destined to be together – if not in this lifetime, then in the future.
reviews.author: Jae-Ha Kim

reviews.text: The film is more literature than cinema, elevated mumblecore for graduate writing seminars, the opposite of, for instance, Hong Sangsoo, who makes low-budget films about writers and filmmakers without worrying about prizes...
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: Never risking discomfort, Song flattens a real-life anecdote of any truly messy feelings, resulting in a tone poem quasi-romance that’s actually serene to a fault. It’s a good movie too chronically polite to achieve anything like greatness.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: Lee concentrates and expresses Nora's state of mind through a marvelous performance in which two feelings that initially seem impossible to transmit simultaneously come together... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Marcelo Stiletano

reviews.text: Past Lives is a treasure and will continue to be for many years.
reviews.author: Dave Giannini

reviews.text: It is a film that is more pretty than profound, it is a film that seeks to present a demonstration based upon speculation: what would have happened if the kids did not separate? [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: The acting was stellar and it's basically about three people but the story is so deep and layered. It's almost a perfect film with saying so much by saying so little.
reviews.author: Justin Brown

reviews.text: I loved this movie. It is a challenging film that makes you reflect on your own personal experiences and that's a testament to how impactful the storytelling and acting is.
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: Past Lives is truly a modern romance, rich with bittersweet understanding of what it means to live in the present.
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: A peaceful and deeply moving work. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juan José Beteta

reviews.text: Vibrates at a very specific emotional pitch that pierced my heart all the way to its core.
reviews.author: Marya E. Gates

reviews.text: This movie is beautifully layered...It's [the film] is so relatable to your life, no matter who you are in terms of partners and past loves...it sticks with you long after you see it. It's definitely worthy of its Best Picture nomination.
reviews.author: Michael Cook

reviews.text: The questions the film raises are simply too fascinating to ignore. Its protagonists do not want to change their present, and yet, deep inside and in an increasingly less subtle way, they cannot stop asking themselves: what if…? Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: There’s no melodrama... Instead, we watch three incredibly lived-in performances guide these characters through a thoughtful, soft-spoken script.
reviews.author: Ross McIndoe

reviews.text: Simple and moving, [Past Lives] is a very interesting debut feature... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Marcelo Paredes

reviews.text: Past Lives tells a story and manages to transcend temporal and physical conventions, conveying the unique magic of a deep connection that defies the restrictions of conventional logic. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juan Pablo Russo

reviews.text: Celice Song reflects upon an avalanche of romantic emotions without ever falling into kitsch. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro Alemán

reviews.text: This is not a bad film, but it is an intensely and conspicuously middle class film.
reviews.author: David Walsh

reviews.text: A nostalgic tribute to those love stories that were left in the pipeline, and with more doubts than answers. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juan Jose Cruz

reviews.text: [Past Lives] asks if a more meaningful and beautiful life might be made by accepting our finitude, keeping commitments, and paring down possibilities.
reviews.author: Morgan Lee

reviews.text: Lilting between Korean and English, Celine Song’s debut feature Past Lives brings an understated but wholly affecting rumination on the immigrant experience.
reviews.author: Pallavi Keswani

reviews.text: By the final scene, you’ll be crying along with Nora.
reviews.author: Josh Kurp

reviews.text: PAST LIVES is a beautiful, deeply touching and tender film. Fantastically played and absolutely captivating visually and musically. Restrained and yet grand.
reviews.author: Jimmy Cage

reviews.text: Past Lives is astute and sharply-observed, emotional without being sentimental. It has lived rent-free in my mind since I saw it six months ago. It’s not to be missed.
reviews.author: Scott Phillips

reviews.text: With all the trappings of a romantic love triangle, the narrative skews toward the less-explored drama: how do we move forward from here? With aspects to cheer for & fear for in each character, this personal production believably bleeds angst & regret...
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: One of recent memory’s most impressive writing and directing debuts.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: It will be remembered as one of the great romantic dramas of the century. It is also a personal story about the experience of emigration, about lost ties and the new identity that is built. About what is left behind. The past lives.
reviews.author: Valentina Morillo

reviews.text: Past Lives is one of those films in which nothing seems to happen, while emotionally all sorts of stuff is going on. The performances are really terrific, with Teo Yoo creating a portrait of sweet longing so heartbreaking you want to give him a hug.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: Too often characters in movies are who they are; they don’t change. It’s a tribute to Song’s crisp and literate script that these are people alive in the moment and in the act of becoming based on where they’ve come from.
reviews.author: James Greenberg

reviews.text: The memories this film presents to the viewer are stuck in the viewer's memory for days and weeks to come.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: The realism is encouraging, astounding, and inspirational, demonstrating just how unusually entertaining a wholesome, unadorned premise about ordinary people can be.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: A deeply emotional experience, the film looks at all the what-ifs in our past relationships and how fate plays a role in our decisions.  Very well-written and acted, this is one to be savored.
reviews.author: Nick Boyd

reviews.text: …cautious, delicate and unsensational, Celine Song’s Past Lives deserves the attention that it’s getting, and it deserves yours too…the subtle mystery outlined provides an ideal focus for self-reflection…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Playwright Celine Song’s filmmaking debut was a devastating reflection on roads not taken.
reviews.author: Chris Klimek

reviews.text: Movies do a lot of things. They entertain, they educate, they make audiences laugh and cry and jump out of their upholstered reclining seats. And on special occasions, they linger.
reviews.author: Ella Feldman

reviews.text: [Past Lives has] the emotional beats and satisfactions of genre romance, but without the happy ending. And it’s glorious.
reviews.author: Noah Berlatsky

reviews.text: What a touching story. A very striking way to look at relationships and the ways that love lingers.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: In Past Lives by playwright and director Celine Song, everything happens with an almost contemplative slowness.  [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Aglaia Berlutti

reviews.text: Is this a film about longing, regret, or an analysis of miscommunication? It's hard to tell as the delivery is so dry and flat.
reviews.author: Alachia Queen

reviews.text: Not only does Song weave together a sophisticated and bittersweet story, she also directs it like someone well beyond their filmmaking years.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: The writing touches the heart in all the best ways, the actors are sublime, and the subtle messaging about identity is fascinating.
reviews.author: Jeanine T. Abraham

reviews.text: Overlooks most of the moments it needs to examine.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: Hollywood romantic icons may be in disrepute, but Greta Lee and Teo Yoo are dull, inexpressive performers whose emotions are as flat as the untrained subjects of a documentary.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: I was especially taken by the performance of Greta Lee and the supporting work of John Magaro.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: It has the singularity of discussing lack of communication, nostalgia and past love in times of urban alienation, but the characters remain in overly sanitized situations that, little by little, dissolve the layer of intimacy.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: The entire film is punctuated by memorable sequences that function as warnings, as signs or, better yet, as clocks. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: With Past Lives, writer and director Song delivers a beautiful and impeccable film where everything is perfectly measured. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Andrea Zamora

reviews.text: In Song's film, delicacy, sensitivity and empathy towards her characters reign. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergi Sánchez

reviews.text: Past Lives does not contribute much more to love, cinema and spirituality than what a luxurious Sunday article in an elegant magazine offers to sophistication.
reviews.author: Javier Ocaña

reviews.text: With such a simple plot, full of silences, looks, and small gestures... in her debut, playwright Celine Song composes a story that speaks of the great evils and good of today, of identity, of frustration. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Irene Crespo

reviews.text: A certainly a well-acted, well directed movie that shows that Celine Song can handle emotion (even sentimentality if you prefer) quite well, in a style that could as well dictate how romantic movies proceed from now on.
reviews.author: Panos Kotzathanasis

reviews.text: It is subtle, not heavy-handed. It is low-key, without gigantic emotional fireworks. There is real emotion, which finally is revealed, but it is just under the surface most of the time. This is a very well-written and acted film.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: This all sounds rather cryptic, and the film is mysterious. It is also lucid and precise, intimately devoted to its strange lyrical sorrow. It’s as if we are watching feelings in slow motion.
reviews.author: Michael Wood

reviews.text: An elegant and unexpectedly mesmerizing character piece that speaks profoundly to the concept of love in the modern age while using an intelligent and ambitious, but still very relatable woman to do so.
reviews.author: Damon Wise

reviews.text: Taking her time to develop characters and relationships, Song deftly brings the audience deep into the narrative until we are fully invested in the eventual outcome.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Ultimately, we are all living the same lives, the same experiences, the same feelings. The film exploits the fact that coincidences don't exist and expands the potential of the eternal human question, "what if?". Masterpiece. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Victor Pineyro

reviews.text: The images and the characters’ spatial relationships within them become such a part of the story that, in the final act, simple moments like an awkward silence at a bar or waiting for an Uber transmit tremendous power.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: Subtle and understated, if occasionally mundane, romantic drama, that reflects our complicated lives in a universal story about the life choices, and sweeps you away in its final climactic moments
reviews.author: Jane Freebury

reviews.text: Past Lives is based above all on two long scenes in which the characters talk, and while they do so, they evoke the wounds of time's passage. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Àngel Quintana

reviews.text: This is, possibly, the film that has shaken me the most in the last decade, and it does so not with exaggerated moments of screams and drama, but with the perfect words to rock you into its small cosmos... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Randy Meeks

reviews.text: Its greatness doesn't so much immediately grab you by the throat but worms its way into your affections more and more with each passing scene, building and building until it becomes impossible to deny in its note-perfect final act.
reviews.author: Ilan Preskovsky

reviews.text: Past Lives is notable for what it leaves out. It is a drama of accommodation, a minimalist romance in which the spectre of a grand passion is held tantalisingly at bay.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: A sublime, aching meditation on memory and time, practical love and idealistic romance, and all the complex contradictions that exist in between.
reviews.author: Farah Cheded

reviews.text: This gorgeous, life-affirming feature is one of the best I’ve seen this year.
reviews.author: Chris Wasser

reviews.text: Past Lives is Song’s first movie, but it feels more like her ninth — it’s wonderfully assured.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Past Lives could battle Oppenheimer at the Oscars. It’s just as explosive.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: Past Lives may be a weepie, but it’s a hyper-sophisticated one.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: Plaudits to the principal cast, who do a miraculous job of portraying inner conflict and ecstasy with the merest tilt of a head, or subtle shift of a shoulder.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: A quietly devastating drama, Past Lives might be one of the early contenders for next year’s Oscars, and is certainly one of the best films you’ll see all year. Watch it before the awards season chatter begins.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Song finds the political in the personal and avoids seeming indulgent or niche.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: The film’s great magic is the way it captures the beauty of lonely cities with a camera that seems to caress their geography.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: There’s a certain tragedy at the heart of this story that no amount of goodwill can soothe: sometimes you don’t get over traumas, you just learn to live with them. But Past Lives, a thoroughly grown-up film, is able to accommodate this inconvenient truth.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Aesthetically, too, the film is gorgeous -- like something you want to reach out and touch.
reviews.author: Daisy Jones

reviews.text: If you are looking for some grown up romance, don’t let Past Lives get away.
reviews.author: Grant Rollings

reviews.text: It’s barely believable that this is Song’s very first feature. Her film is simply sublime from start to finish.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: It is highly recommended as a touching and always subtle film about old memories, old friendships and contemporary realities.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: The performances are impossibly strong and awards-season ready. Anything other than a best actress Oscar nomination for Lee will be criminal.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: It is a film that embraces blended nationalities while acknowledging the pull of one’s earliest home. One leaves aware of unavoidable open-endedness but sated by a work that has achieved all its lofty ambitions.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Past Lives isn’t quite the woozy, lovelorn drama that its trailers have sold... But it is an eloquent attempt to understand how our memories can end up turning other people into projection screens for our own, confused desires.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Past Lives is breathtaking, leaving you speechless in the most wonderful way.
reviews.author: Paula Farmer

reviews.text: A little movie with the biggest of hearts, Past Lives heralds the arrival of playwright turned director Céline Song as a filmmaker with the brightest of futures. It's the most charming of debuts, and if you miss it, your screen life will be the poorer.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: There is always a forward momentum to the film even when nothing much seems to be happening. All the scenario's emotional complexity, though, is articulated by the actors’ expressions.
reviews.author: Helen Hawkins

reviews.text: That it’s exquisitely affecting and made with great precision and care is enough for now. No need to make a song and dance about it. Indeed, as Past Lives so deftly shows, you can have an excellent drama without any of the drama.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: I've never quite seen a love story or a friendship bond told on screen like Past Lives, I was enthralled  with the film, easily one of the best of the year.
reviews.author: Lauren Veneziani

reviews.text: It’s a must-see.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Past Lives is not only a breath-taking debut by Celine Song, it is a herald to an astounding voice in cinema.
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

reviews.text: Past Lives is naggingly unsatisfying: the characters are not fully realised, and nor is their story. The film anticipates an impact it doesn’t earn.
reviews.author: Ann Manov

reviews.text: A transcendent debut for South Korean-Canadian filmmaker Celine Song, this romantic drama is a masterclass in slow, simmering storytelling. It will stay with you, maybe even into your next life.
reviews.author: Nick De Semlyen

reviews.text: Celine Song’s directorial debut is a beautiful story of friendship & contemplation about the choices we make in life. It is powerfully relatable and the film shows us that it’s okay to be sad about the road not taken without having regrets.
reviews.author: Patrick Hicks

reviews.text: In Past Lives, director Celine Song twists the knife on the all-too-familiar romantic woes that Asian immigrants like myself endure: the slow yet gut-wrenching impact of long-distance relationships and our complex relationship with fate.
reviews.author: Ryan Oquiza

reviews.text: A tender and mesmerising romance with an absolutely sensational lead performance from Lee.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: It is a movie that carries the weight of years upon its shoulders, of ineffable longing and the possibility of cosmic alignment, but it does so with a cinematic spring in its step.
reviews.author: Petr Navovy

reviews.text: The film's directness, its relative storytelling simplicity, is also its asset. Past Lives unravels at a rhythm that weaves a slow-burning spell, one that allows an audience the space to project their own experience onto the screen.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: The masterstroke of Song’s screenplay is that, despite its emotional directness, there is still ample room to reinterpret character dynamics up to and including the devastating final moments.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: The bittersweet reconnecting of childhood soulmates wraps an unrealised love story in unanswerable questions.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: One of the best written screenplays for a long, long time. It has a Woody Allen feel to it that just makes it a masterpiece.
reviews.author: David Griffiths

reviews.text: It’s quite the remarkable first film for Song, who brings a tender, elegant economy to her storytelling that doesn’t quite prepare you for how much it’ll wipe you out at the closing stretch. This one aches really good, folks. I can’t shake it.
reviews.author: Aaron Yap

reviews.text: Like few others, Past Lives shows the cultural and emotional dichotomy of those of us who have left our countries of origin and never completely detach ourselves from them, no matter how many years go by... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gustavo Herrera Taboada

reviews.text: For this is as much a story of her [Nora] wrestling with the importance of her Korean heritage, as it is any romantic notions of fate, destiny or, as the Koreans call it, in-yun.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: A small, sweet but ultimately soulful film, a triumph for Celine Song and a beautifully unwrapped gift for audiences.
reviews.author: Liam Macleod

reviews.text: … starts slow but then ramps up into an absolute stunner of a romantic drama, populated by fleshed-out and endlessly likeable characters who explore deeply relatable aspects of loves and lives that could have been.
reviews.author: Cain Noble-Davies

reviews.text: Every shot is well-considered, every line of dialogue neatly parsed, each performance exquisitely choreographed to convey a thoroughly conceived idea in a naturalistic style. It’s a lovely, lovely film, and one of the year’s best.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: A love story that will linger on your mind for a long, long to come.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: This delicate and eloquent meditation on destiny and choice is an emotional experience, beautifully played.
reviews.author: Whang Yee Ling

reviews.text: This is the real deal. If you’ve an interest in five-star contemporary cinema, you miss this at your peril.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: This is a film that understands the dopamine rush of digital connection, but also the way it can be used to prolong the blissed-out potential of a relationship by repeatedly deferring a real-world encounter.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: [F]or all the talk of in-yun, the true past life is the one Nora left behind in Korea[.]
reviews.author: CJ Sheu

reviews.text: Celine Song’s tender, time-spanning romance is an exquisitely judged wonder. A directorial debut of remarkable poise and power.
reviews.author: Matt Maytum

reviews.text: Past Lives should not be missed.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: It’s fine for a movie not to spell everything out, in fact, it’s preferable. But in Past Lives, Nora’s opacity left me uninvolved at times.
reviews.author: Hannah Brown

reviews.text: Past Lives is a film about time, missed opportunities and enduring connections, and Song ably juxtaposes private reflection with romantic longing.
reviews.author: Asher Luberto

reviews.text: Past Lives is the epitome of contemplative, meditative cinema.
reviews.author: Tynan Yanaga

reviews.text: Song’s masterful direction and ability to tell a story mostly visually make Past Lives a masterpiece. It’s an eloquent, alluring film about what we leave behind and what we gain from it.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: There’s something transcendent about this story, which captures the bigness of human existence in a way that leaves you in awe, and maybe helps you understand love and loss and life a little better.
reviews.author: Tim Miller

reviews.text: Culturally specific yet universally resonant, this bittersweet Korean drama is a quietly perceptive and deeply profound look at unspoken relationship bonds.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Past Lives is a heartrending and deeply felt examination of two souls linked together, that while leaving an enduring impact on each other’s lives, are destined to be apart.
reviews.author: Mark Johnson

reviews.text: “Who do you think they are to each other?” The question echoes as the film’s ending returns to the bar where it was initially asked. Perhaps a better question is, what does it mean to know someone?
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: Past Lives is a sonic-visual feast in the service of a deeply moving, revelatory treatise on subtle human truths...it’s easily one of the best films of the year, if not, the best.
reviews.author: Prabhjot Bains

reviews.text: Celine Song presents an intimate and delicate three-decade-spanning portrait of the importance people play in our lives that resembles Richard Linklater’s Before trilogy.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text: Past Lives is a emotional experience like no other! Nearly every moment in this film felt real and layered with so many earnest emotions, and it captures that haunting and heartbreaking reality of “what if” PERFECTLY!
reviews.author: Elliott Collins

reviews.text: Past Lives is schematic but effective; what makes it work are the performances by Greta Lee and Teo Yoo as these star-crossed not-quite lovers’ adolescent and adult incarnations.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: Past Lives is the sort of thing that might blow a hole in your chest if you hold regrets about roads not taken.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: A24’s Past Lives is a masterpiece & lives up to everything you’ve heard about it already. Truly a romance for the ages that will break your heart, bring it back together, & then touch your soul.
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Past Lives is quietly powerful – an understated examination of longing, connection, and unconsummated love.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: The tug of Past Lives is situated in the many moments that come together to shape the film into a meaningful whole about love—lost and found, abandoned and claimed.
reviews.author: Namrata Joshi

reviews.text: It celebrates the people who leave an indelible mark, regardless of time and distance. What's truly astonishing is how a film this levelheaded can still break your heart into a million tiny pieces.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: Whether you find Past Lives mesmerizing or not, its portrait of relationships rings true -- and could inspire bouts of soul searching.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: Nary a dishonest note to be found in this mesmerizing film.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: An absolutely beautiful film, that never collapses into cliche.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: As Nora, Greta Lee, gives a complex, nuanced performance that understates and fully reveals the depth of her emotions.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: Past Lives is one of those rare films that charms audiences with its subtle beauty but wins them over with its immense intelligence and heart.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: "[Celine] Song knows that sometimes to preserve the purity of an eternal love story is to leave it incomplete. After all, believers in romance will often tell you, there’s always a next life."
reviews.author: Tatsam Mukherjee

reviews.text: Past Lives has an autobiographical touch and offers a memorable cinematic experience well worth having.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Past Lives is an emotional powerhouse. It's a romance that’s not meant to be, and a film built on the immigrant experience and the power of empathy and honesty in difficult situations.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: A bitingly poignant film about heartache, time, longing, childhood friendship and finding closure.
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: PAST LIVES is sexy and funny and tender along its seemingly familiar path, but it never ignores the mundane truth that destiny, more often than not, keeps people apart. Reality isn't a fairy tale.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: It is an embrace of every hitch and hiccup, every misstep and missed opportunity that led you to be who you are. It is a dirge, an elegy for who others saw you to be but who you never were. It is an innocent idea, a dangerous daydream, a painful pleasure.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: The MVP here is John Magaro, who delivers a quietly devastating performance as Nora’s husband, Arthur.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: It is an honest introspection that explores gut-wrenching concepts of regret and destiny, asking us to ponder the consequences of choices.
reviews.author: Neil Soans

reviews.text: Bookended by two departures, Celine Song’s delicate debut Past Lives, in which a woman finds herself torn between two men, is less about the longing for someone you moved away from and more about the version of yourself that you left behind with them.
reviews.author: Gayle Sequeira

reviews.text: Song juggles so many tricky and often conflicting emotions, then deftly wraps them in a delicate but devastating package. It's a dreamy, melancholy, and altogether remarkable debut.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Practical, logical, and infinitely moving in its humanity. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: It’s not about “taking the road less travelled” as Frost would tell with a sigh, but the road not taken that keeps the traveller thinking what could have been.
reviews.author: Diana Cheng

reviews.text: Celine Song's impressive debut film is so beautiful, and so heartbreaking. Its quite the achievement. The pace, writing, cinematography, music, acting, and what it explores: simply gorgeous. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Past Lives soars! Writer and director Celine Strong’s debut is a love story of jaw-dropping maturity.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: A refreshing film in its celebration of moral restraint, self-denial, and sticking with commitments in a world where the opposite is often encouraged, or at least deemed more “authentic.”
reviews.author: Brett McCracken

reviews.text: Its most devastating conversations play out in the intimate confines of an apartment, in a quiet bar where confessions come gently tumbling out or on a dimly lit street that becomes a liminal space. And yet, these moments are not small at all.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: Past Lives is moving, inspiring, and honest. There is so much emotion and care put into each aspect of the film, it is self-evident. I loved spending time with these characters, and I look forward to revisiting this again in my next life.
reviews.author: Ryan Silberstein

reviews.text: ...a watchable yet rarely involving drama that remains unable to wholeheartedly capture the viewer’s interest and attention...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: “Past Lives” is absolutely the kind of film that makes you want to discuss it with other people, not because of some insane plot twists or theories, but because it speaks to personal experiences in a deep and nuanced way.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: Though Past Lives is an epic in scope spanning decades at its core it’s a sweet intimate drama about how your past colors your present and often clouds your future.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: Past Lives is lovely—smart, deeply felt, carefully observed, pleasingly patient with its characters and their emotions.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: Past Lives is the year’s other great multiverse movie.
reviews.author: Adam Kempenaar

reviews.text: The trio’s performances are pitch-perfect, and nobody is designed to be a hero or villain, just adults trying to be sincere and pragmatic. At a crossroads in their lives, they all express yearning, yet from distinctive viewpoints.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: Though its laid back pacing and slice-of-life approach to narrative may make the first hour feel particularly lengthy, the emotional potency of Past Lives is undeniable.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: In Song's impossibly adept debut, she's able to find balance and harmony in the chaos of an ever-surging society.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: Celine Song's debut feature is a beautiful and contemplative look at identity, expectation, and what could've been. Small but important nuances weave a well rounded picture of a question we all have asked ourselves at one point, "what would've been?"
reviews.author: Dana Han-Klein

reviews.text: It wouldn’t be a hyperbole to call Past Lives a perfect film. Absolutely spellbinding, never has something so low-key hit me like a ton of bricks.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: A deeply romantic film that isn't really about romance per se, it has sort of screenplay that can only come from lived experience and keen observation.
reviews.author: Andrew Wyatt

reviews.text: It's a deep, resonant, intimate story which unfolds naturalistically and at a soulful pace.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Direct, deeply personal and emotionally piercing...a romantic triangle that remains poised between unresolved longing and what might have been—and what might be in the future.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: These characters aren’t looking to blow up their lives for the sake of movie contrivances, but through every private conversation, they’re drawn to discussing the same narrative possibilities on the audience’s minds.
reviews.author: Chance Solem-Pfeifer

reviews.text: A deeply emotionally mature film in which happily ever after isn’t guaranteed. Majestic.
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: Told with incredible depth, cinematic magnetism and emotional authenticity, 'Past Lives' is a beautiful story about being adrift in what-ifs.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Ultimately what takes Past Lives to another level is Lee. It's the best performance of 2023 to date as Lee manages to convey her character's inner struggles a lot of time with nothing more than a glance or facial reaction.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: This is the kind of movie that sets up a pup tent in your brain and never really leaves, drawing you gently back every so often.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: It seems most critics are responding to its subject matter, the ideas about missed opportunities and what-ifs ... I couldn’t find the cinematic oomph that would make those ideas come to full life.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: In this leisurely, graceful, mesmerizing romance, the magnetic Lee navigates between the past and the present, pragmatism and magical possibilities.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: Past Lives is deceptively unrestrained in its exploration of how we decide what we were meant to do and who we were meant to be with, and the acceptable regret that comes even when we've made a good choice.
reviews.author: Shelagh Rowan-Legg

reviews.text: No movie this year shows the hurt of lost dreams like Past Lives.
reviews.author: Daniel Eagan

reviews.text: Past Lives feels so deliciously restrained that it makes even quiet dramas seem histrionic. And yet it’s a wide emotional field that gives its characters room to breathe... if Past Lives isn’t 2023’s best film, we’re in for an incredible year of cinema.
reviews.author: John Wenzel

reviews.text: Grief, albeit perhaps gentle, inevitably accompanies the sadness of unsatisfied yearnings and roads not taken. Even if past and future lives are possible, we still must live them one at a time.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: “Past Lives” plays to the aching hearts crowd, with Song serving up a romance novel premise with an art-house film approach, capturing a specific pitch of yearning.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: You’ll find your heart filling, swelling and yearning in this thought-provoking, full-of-feels tale about the choices we make, the choices that make us, what we did, what we didn’t do, and what we might have done.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: It’s a movie of poetic dialogue, but we fill the silences with our own reminiscing about who we’ve become and who we might have been.
reviews.author: David Lynch

reviews.text: [It's] a remarkable movie, bittersweet and quietly philosophical.
reviews.author: Gena Radcliffe

reviews.text: Celine Song has delivered one of the best films of 2023.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: A quiet, contemplative but emotionally torrid look at a romance that never was. Filmmaker Celine Song dazzles with her mature vision of true longing and the choices we make.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: Teens who are used to fast cuts, expressive reactions, and entertainment that gets to the point won't find any of those in the contemplative Past Lives.
reviews.author: Tara McNamara

reviews.text: Delicately drifts between romance and regret...
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Underneath its burning romantic exterior lies a complex, symmetrical study of seeking closure with your first love and the childhood you left behind. Past Lives is an all-time great that deserves to be seen in this life.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: A beautiful and nuanced personal expression by Song that considers how the past is written on our lives, no matter how hard we try to erase it.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: “Past Lives” is a great movie. One that you shouldn’t miss.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: It’s a film full of quiet magic; of the power of words not spoken, and the enduring strength of love.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: Song’s directorial debut is a masterpiece of emotional restraint revealing multiple sides of love. Song hand-picked the cast which excels portraying this gripping story that has its light moments as well as intense drama in a clash of cultures over time.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: This is a touching weepie romancer, that is so well-done on all levels.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: As a writer, Song’s lovely screenplay keeps the tension free of rom-com contrivances. As a director, her keen eye, attention to detail and artful framing announce an exciting new filmmaker.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Burning slow and composing its emotions until it knows when to release them in a flood of responsive passion, [Celine] Song’s impeccable debut is a drama of humanism and quiet complexity.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: It's is a shrewdly low-key and delicate examination of love, one that leaves quiet devastation in its wake. You’ll come away feeling inspired by a great filmmaker and wholly affected by her incredibly affecting love story.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: One really feels so enraptured by the themes of fate, love, and free will that what’s being expertly set up leaves you speechless.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: A gentle and tender movie about the life we leave behind when we immigrate, and how we embalm those memories in rose-colored hues, told through a relationship filled with longing.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: A confident entry in the canon of great romances—one that expands the emotional scope of what a love story can be.
reviews.author: Shirley Li

reviews.text: Past Lives is a work of remarkable delicacy and humor about fate, connections, and the narratives we event for our lives.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Lyrical, potent, well-acted, and the year's best movie thus far.
reviews.author: Matthew St. Clair

reviews.text: Song masterfully simplifies things on an emotional level, allowing us to switch back and forth between feelings or simply to meditate on the outcome we wish for, and to understand why it’s OK if we don’t get it.
reviews.author: Odie Henderson

reviews.text: A thoughtful and realistic love story of two passing ships in the night.
reviews.author: Rachel Ho

reviews.text: The captivating and rarified results from Celine Song show mature restraint, reward patience, and disarm all sympathies for living and being alive.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: [Greta] Lee and [Teo] Yoo are electric together, conveying an excess of feelings both unspoken and not fully understood through their graceful exchange of looks and dialogue.
reviews.author: Trace Sauveur

reviews.text: Celine Song's powerful debut film touches the soul with an intimate story about fate and the mysteries of love and life. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: Song’s grace in the film is found through her empathic understanding of how even the briefest relationship can take up space in a person’s heart for decades.
reviews.author: Allyson Johnson

reviews.text: Emphasizes the ones that got away … which become the fantasy vs. the reality. How do we define love, in the age or generation we’re in? This story tries to get to that definition, and is a must see for the empathy and commonality in all of our life times.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: A radiant work of delicate artistry, unfolding at the nexus of personal and cultural experience, and unfurling the secret worlds that exist within each mind, body and soul, yielding a shattering tale of nostalgic self-reflection and the passage of time.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: Past Lives takes audiences through the emotional roller coaster of the Before trilogy with the economy of Brief Encounter. There’s not a wasted second here, as is the case with loves that define our lives whether they stay or go.
reviews.author: Pat Mullen

reviews.text: The strength of the ... [film] is in how many deeper questions Song leaves us with, even after her film answers those most obvious, seemingly pertinent questions.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Song must truly be a marvel of a playwright, because her dialogue carefully builds on the tiny details which amount to what it means to truly see and respect a person.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: The poetic lyricism Song layers in with major assists from cinematographer Shabier Kirchner and editor Keith Fraase never seems like mere filigree. It’s the cinematic language that helps a story...
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: Celine Song makes a quietly spectacular writing-directing debut with Past Lives, a lyrical slow burn of a film that expertly holds back wellsprings of emotion, until it unleashes a deluge.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: It’s a rare movie that settles, quietly, into some part of your own experiences and memories without a speck of narrative contrivance gumming up your response to the story on the screen.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: It’s impossible to heap enough praise upon Past Lives. The movie is so calm and quiet but screaming with emotional depth and complexity. None of it would be possible without the perfect cast and scripting to go with each of them.
reviews.author: Jason Flatt

reviews.text: Past Lives treats these very human characters with respect and care, and in turn we care for all of them.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: Like all of the best works of cinema, Past Lives finds a vein of untapped potential in places often undefined and under-explored and mines every bit of truth it can from those spaces that linger in the memory, but are often hardest to put into words.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: Song’s film [is] a strong debut feature with the occasional staginess that reveals her playwright origins.
reviews.author: Peter Keough

reviews.text: Past Lives may not be the movie you might expect from all the raves and best-of-the-year predictions. That’s fitting considering how so much of this film is very much about the death of expectations.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: Through a prismatic portrait of unrequited love, fate, identity and timing, this deft, low-key exploration of a decades-spanning kismet spark acts as a soothing balm and leaves us feeling like a puddle of mushy goo.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: As the story unfolds, we watch these three lives intertwine in unexpected ways. It is a satisfying debut from a new talent.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Celine Song’s Past Lives is the kind of movie that seems simple, but is thematically rich, expertly crafted and will wow you when all is said and done.
reviews.author: Michael Balderston

reviews.text: An achingly beautiful, emotionally subtle and understatedly powerful film.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: At its essence, this is a film for anyone who’s ever known the ache of “the one who got away” and “what-if.”
reviews.author: Hannah Bae

reviews.text: Listening to Celine Song’s dialogue, we’re reminded by just how rare it is to hear honest adult conversations like this in film, ones that don’t shout or grandstand but burrow into the emotions in the subtlest of ways.
reviews.author: Jay Weissberg

reviews.text: Achieves ardent and authentic emotional voyeurism ... "Will they? Won't they?" We could live in a purgatory this sumptuous for much longer than 106 minutes.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: This is a film containing oceans of truth, centuries of longing and vast feelings of open-hearted tenderness.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Celine Song's masterful debut transcends our deepest desires and will resurrect the long dormant feelings we have all had from time to time or the fear of losing the best person we have ever known.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: For some, the film could lack incident, but that’s what makes it so special. By declining to move her story into the realm of melodrama, Song creates a truly immersive emotional experience.
reviews.author: Tanner Gordon

reviews.text: Writer/director Celine Song, a playwright making her feature debut, tells a simple but emotionally rich story based on her own experience of a connection interrupted but never broken, a sentimental tale in the true sense of the word.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Without sacrificing its slender sense of flow, Past Lives is especially astute in articulating all the forces — culture, language, time, fate, love, and connection — that overlap to form the possibilities of her characters’ lives.
reviews.author: Isaac Feldberg

reviews.text: There’s a disconcerting shrewdness underneath its patina of tastefulness — it’s too calculating to achieve the transcendent almost-romance it strives for but never inhabits.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Celine Song’s debut film is, without a doubt, one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Maxwell Rabb

reviews.text: Past Lives is a quietly observed but intimately studied film that really sticks with you.
reviews.author: Terence Johnson

reviews.text: A movie that liberates your tears and makes you fall in love with it. It is almost assuredly predestined to be the single best movie you see this year.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: Song has said the film is semiautobiographical, and it shows. Although at times technically wayward and dramatically diffuse, there is not a moment in it that does not bear the personal stamp of a lived-in connection.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: Past Lives plays with your brain and your heart. It’s one of those films that leaves you thinking about and maybe yearning for what might have been.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: With a star-making turn from Greta Lee, Past Lives might just be the best romance of the 21st century.
reviews.author: Audrey Fox

reviews.text: It’s so rare to see a movie like Past Lives, one in which every detail is so perfectly defined by writer/director Celine Song.
reviews.author: Liz Shannon Miller

reviews.text: There is destiny, and then there is inyeon (or in-yeon). It’s one of those beautiful non-English words that hardly translates from its native language. But after watching Past Lives, you’ll never forget the meaning of it.
reviews.author: Allegra Frank

reviews.text: Song and her first-rate cast take the “still waters run deep” understated approach. The result is at once straightforward and old-fashioned, yet contemporary. In doing so, Song has single-handedly reenergized a genre.
reviews.author: Kent Turner

reviews.text: Past Lives [is] the calm, clear-eyed filmmaking debut of the New York-based, Korean-American playwright Celine Song.
reviews.author: Matthew Eng

reviews.text: The movie ripples with the quiet melodrama of real life, the way big things often happen in the margins, and small things gradually come to mean the world.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: This is an instantly great piece of cinema and a breakout film for Celine Song. Past Lives is fantastic now, later, in this life, and the next.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Past Lives, folding two decades into less than two hours, is as swift and fleet as it is emotionally and philosophically expansive.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: [Celine] Song’s adroit writing and the hard work of actors Teo Yoo and the steely Greta Lee culminate in an emotional denouement as satisfying as it is devastating.
reviews.author: Oliver Jones

reviews.text: Besides announcing Song as a brilliant observer of dialogue, interaction, and tone, Past Lives is a strikingly romantic movie about what composes our lives.
reviews.author: Jacob Oller

reviews.text: This is a well-acted, well-told story, with sneakily impressive filmmaking to further emphasize the strength of this narrative.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Heads up, Oscar. Celine Song  crafts the best movie of the year so far by using her own life to explore the meaning of destiny as a Korean playwright (the glorious Greta Lee) is torn between a past love (Teo Yoo) and her American husband (John Magaro).
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: In an electrifyingly alive debut feature, writer/director Celine Song delivers the kind of movie you don't just nestle into but long to revisit. And yes, it's likely one of the very best films of 2023.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: The film hits home. In part, that is a tribute to its melancholy.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: This steady and luxuriantly languid film moves at the pace of longing, what if, and maybe love—-but it is also uncomfortable for me, as though something precious is falling apart and I am a voyeur to its demise
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: Past Lives beautifully tells a mature and realistic story about love, friendship, and heartbreak for two people whose lives have gone in different directions, but they find a way to reconnect. It’s a relationship drama that’s an instant classic
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: Song draws you into her characters’ worlds seamlessly.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: Technology functions almost like a translator, allowing Nora and Hae Sung digital windows into their past selves that aren’t as static as simply flipping through old photos. Yet there are only so many miracles technology can perform.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: Celine Song's directional debut is like an emotional boomerang centered within young love and pining for the one person you feel destined to for eternity.  Greta Lee and Teo Yoo have a chemistry that permeates even without dialogue
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: A masterclass in storytelling.
reviews.author: Monica Castillo

reviews.text: The emotions are likely to wash over you without you even realizing how much the story is affecting you.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: The film affords viewers who’ve ever spent years chasing dreams the chance to pause and ponder – perhaps in the absence of a visitor from the past – whether we’ve meaningfully changed who we are or we’ve only successfully crafted façades.
reviews.author: Martin Tsai

reviews.text: The treatment of time, which is stretched and pulled, crumpled, torn and put back together, makes “Past Lives” a deeply meditative and existentially curious piece.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Past Lives might not always tackle the newest of emotions but no one can deny the effectiveness of the conversation that does happen on screen.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: 'Past Lives' teaches us that old lovers and friends can often lead us back to a forgotten part of ourselves – even if they aren’t meant to be more than a memory.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: It’s the definition of a tearjerker, something so lived-in without a single dishonest second, and one of the most relatable romances anyone will ever see in their lives. Everyone should see it in every life
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Wise, honest and genuinely heartfelt. It's destined to become a classic love story.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: A great movie, period.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: Writer-director Celine Song brilliantly explores so many specific and intricate areas of the heart that she may as well call herself a cardiologist.
reviews.author: Cody Dericks

reviews.text: the rawness that the lead actors wear in their performances elevate the film and confirm Song as one of the most exciting screenwriting dramatists since Florian Zeller burst on the scene with 2020’s The Father.
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: Song makes it all feel so natural and real, allowing an outsider’s glimpse into this simmering relationship to blossom into something closer to deep knowing and genuine intimacy.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: An achingly lovely debut. Song’s touch is deft, delicate and it sure gets a little dusty in the auditorium at the end.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: Life experience makes me judge them more harshly than do the film's director...I would have preferred not to have spent two hours with either of them.
reviews.author: Amy Taubin

reviews.text: With Past Lives, director Celine Song has a fine story on her hands — and she knows it. Unfortunately, a solid story hook is about all Past Lives amounts to, lacking as it does any robust cinematic interest.
reviews.author: Lawrence Garcia

reviews.text: A perfect movie. “Past Lives” is flawless. Do not miss it under any circumstances.
reviews.author: Sarah Manvel

reviews.text: With a slight hand and amazing dialogue, Past Lives goes beyond its premise to deliver reflections that are not typical and that give the film a hidden force that's interesting and essential to discover: the theme of migration. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: How can anyone put into words all the emotions & feelings that one person has for another? It's impossible. No spoken language on this planet has the right words to describe all those feelings and their nuances. There is, however, the language of cinema.
reviews.author: Alex Billington

reviews.text: If Celine Song’s Past Lives allows men and women to break out of gender expectations, John Trengrove’s Manodrome holds out an olive branch to the kind of alpha men who use the gym as a place of validation.
reviews.author: Shubhra Gupta

reviews.text: Captivating and profoundly moving...
reviews.author: Zhuo-Ning Su

reviews.text: Past Lives is layered, nuanced, and whole at the same time and in its singularity maybe there is the hope to counter the necessarily fragmented human nature.
reviews.author: Savina Petkova

reviews.text: Neither melodramatic nor maudlin, Song’s poetic precision conveys experiences we may all be familiar with but are often the most difficult to express so astutely, if only because we are so inarticulate in the communication or processing of such emotions.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: Tender and moving, Past Lives will touch the depths of your soul with its honesty and integrity.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: An effective encapsulation of the complexities of diaspora and multicultural relationships.
reviews.author: Rafaela Sales Ross

reviews.text: Making an utterly assured feature debut, writer-director Celine Song modulates the delicate tonal balance of this wise, wistful film perfectly.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: Diverging from romances in which lovers are expected to move heaven, earth, and themselves in order to make a moment of love last forever, Past Lives asks us to embrace the changes that come with time.
reviews.author: Pat Brown

reviews.text: Past Lives makes time for the minutiae that define the immigrant experience.
reviews.author: Murtada Elfadl

reviews.text: Telling a delicate tale about missed connections, what ifs and the parts of ourselves we keep buried within, Past Lives might just be the most singularly exquisite film of this year’s Sundance.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: Song’s work here is incredible, as this story of the past and present, and what it means for the future is a carefully handled story told with love and heart.
reviews.author: Ross Bonaime

reviews.text: For what it is, it does tell a bittersweet love story well, but I just found it stressful to watch.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: As the credits roll, viewers may find themselves with only one word floating through their minds then gently escaping their lips: “woah”.
reviews.author: Thomas Stoneham-Judge

reviews.text: It’s a minor film in its scope and structure, and yet it feels so very major.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: Past Lives perfectly captures the shared feeling of melancholic longing between two souls. It basks us in the yearning for forbidden love better than any film I’ve seen this decade.
reviews.author: Wael Khairy

reviews.text: A delicate, touching, stunner of a debut film with astonishingly honest and real writing.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Fueled by possibilities, pining, and yearning, Past Lives is one of the best films to come out in recent years.
reviews.author: Josie Meléndez

reviews.text: An achingly emotional Korean relationship drama about fate, pursuing dreams, regrets, and finding happiness where you are.
reviews.author: Aaron White

reviews.text: It’s a movie that understands how yearning lives in your body even when you think you’ve set it aside.
reviews.author: Nicolas Rapold

reviews.text: January isn’t usually the time to start making Top 10 lists, but I can already confidently put Past Lives on mine.
reviews.author: Sam Adams

reviews.text: “Past Lives” is based on events in the director’s own life, and it has the quiet impact of home truths.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: An exquisite original.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: Past Lives is a miraculous little film from A24, steady and slow and haunted, in the existential sense, by possibilities.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: An exquisitely wistful drama that speaks with an honesty so affectingly crisp it will turn your conceptions of love, identity and fate on their head.
reviews.author: Carlos Aguilar

reviews.text: The story is simple, but there is beauty in its layers, its performances & the heart-wrenching & deeply moving connection between its characters.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: Past Lives is destined to be one of the best movies of 2023.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: It’s a warm, patient film culminating in a quietly powerful, reflective finale, though its sum is greater than its parts when the first two sections register a touch underdeveloped.
reviews.author: Jordan Raup

reviews.text: It is a very tough thing indeed to make a film that is at once restrained and brimming with feeling, a movie that could be fairly described as both big and small.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Few are the films that offer such revelatory conversations between men and women.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: [A] delicate yet crushingly beautiful film...
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: It’s a beautiful, transporting film but one made with both feet firmly on the ground.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

synopsis: Nora and Hae Sung, two deeply connected childhood friends, are wrest apart after Nora's family emigrates from South Korea. Two decades later, they are reunited in New York for one fateful week as they confront notions of destiny, love, and the choices that make a life, in this heartrending modern romance.
